subsegment: Onshore wind farm — utility-scale (60-100 turbines, 150-400 MW)
description: Utility-scale onshore wind generation projects on agricultural or rangeland sites, typically structured as fixed-price EPC with separate turbine supply agreements (TSA) wrapped under the EPC. Schedule is dominated by tax-credit safe-harbor windows and seasonal access constraints.

typical_risks.description_template: Single-source nacelle supply from {oem} exposes schedule to factory delivery slippage; nacelle bottleneck would defer COD beyond PTC safe-harbor window.
COD must precede IRA tax-credit step-down on {deadline_date}; any 4+ week slip materially erodes project economics for owner and triggers LDs.
Caisson and spread-footing designs assumed competent bedrock at <8m; site investigation across {n_turbines} pads may reveal variable depth-to-rock requiring redesign.
Specialised LR-series crawler crane crews are regionally scarce during peak wind construction season; mobilisation slip cascades into turbine erection sequence.
Sustained winds above 11 m/s and icing conditions prevent main-component lifts; {region} historical data suggests 6-10 week erection blackout from December to February.
USFWS eagle take permit conditions impose seasonal construction restrictions; non-compliance triggers permit suspension and stop-work.
Network upgrade scope on the {utility} side may shift through SIS/Facilities Study revisions, exposing schedule to transmission owner delivery dates outside EPC control.
Crossing agreements with {n_landowners} parcel owners along collection lines may produce localised access denials forcing route revisions.

typical_issues.description_template: State DOT oversize-load permit for blade delivery delayed, holding turbine erection sequence.
Domestic rebar lead time extended; foundation pour sequence at risk for next 4 weeks.
Met tower SCADA outage during commissioning created a wind data gap requiring extended performance test window.
Two MV collection cable splice failures detected during energisation; remediation across affected runs in progress.
GSU transformer ex-works date slipped by {n_weeks} weeks; substation backfeed sequence rebaselined.
Heavy rain caused crane pad subgrade failure at pads {pad_ids}; remediation and re-survey required before next lift.
Recordable injury during nacelle internal work; stand-down completed, root cause under investigation.
Turbine-level punch list closure lagging COD requirement; warranty handover at risk.
FAA-compliant obstruction lighting controller firmware issue delaying final acceptance.
Initial PPA capacity test underperformed by {pct}%; investigation into curtailment and curve underperformance underway.

typical_co_drivers: Owner-directed turbine model upgrade mid-procurement
Interconnection network upgrade scope additions from utility re-study
Differing site conditions at foundation locations requiring redesign
Collection line re-routing around late-identified wetland or cultural resource
Acceleration directive to preserve tax-credit COD window

subsegment: Utility-scale solar PV — single-axis tracker (50-250 MWac)
description: Greenfield PV plants on flat agricultural or desert land, with optional DC-coupled BESS scope. Fixed-price EPC with module supply often owner-furnished or carved out; schedule risk concentrated around tracker delivery and interconnection.

typical_risks.description_template: Module shipments may be detained under UFLPA enforcement at port of entry; release timelines from CBP are unpredictable and can delay mechanical completion.
Single tracker vendor {tracker_oem} supplies torque tubes, drives, and controls; any quality hold cascades across {n_blocks} blocks.
Placed-in-service must precede the IRA bonus credit step-down; substation backfeed dependency on utility is the critical schedule chain.
Pile driving across {n_acres} acres may encounter refusal in caliche or rock layers, requiring pre-drilling for a percentage of {pile_count} piles.
Concurrent regional solar build-out pressures journeyman electrician availability; ramp curve for DC and MV terminations at risk.
Site in {region} hail-alley exposes installed modules to in-construction hail damage; stow algorithm and insurance coverage gaps may be exposed.
Owner-furnished module substitution mid-construction triggers re-stamping of structural and electrical calculations and tracker re-configuration.

typical_issues.description_template: Container of modules held at port pending UFLPA documentation review; {n_mw} MW of installation deferred.
Pile refusal rate exceeded {pct}% in north sectors; pre-drill rig mobilised, productivity impact under quantification.
Central inverter firmware fails utility witness test; vendor field engineer dispatched.
QC found row-to-row alignment outside spec across {n_blocks} blocks; rework planned during low-wind windows.
Regional wildfire smoke reducing crew hours under company AQI policy.
Trencher damaged previously installed MV cable; repair and re-test ongoing.
DGA results on GSU transformer show elevated gases during energisation; vendor investigation in progress.
Heavy rainfall overwhelmed sediment controls; CGP corrective action notice expected.
Artifact discovered during civil works; tribal monitor consultation paused work in affected area.
Initial capacity test PR below contractual threshold by {pct}%; soiling and string-level diagnostics underway.

typical_co_drivers: Owner-directed module technology change (bifacial / larger format)
BESS scope addition or capacity increase post-NTP
Differing subsurface conditions requiring pre-drill or ballasted foundations
Interconnection facility scope additions from utility
Acceleration to preserve ITC/PIS deadline

subsegment: Run-of-river hydroelectric — small to mid-scale (10-50 MW)
description: Low-head or medium-head run-of-river hydro with weir, intake, penstock, and powerhouse. Schedule and cost are dominated by in-water work windows, FERC licensing conditions, and geotechnical surprises in tunnel or penstock alignments.

typical_risks.description_template: Francis/Kaplan turbine-generator package from {oem} on critical path; factory acceptance test delays propagate to wet commissioning.
License Articles impose minimum flow, ramping, and fish passage conditions during construction; non-compliance risks suspension orders.
Tunnel alignment crosses {n_zones} fault and shear zones; actual rock quality may diverge from baseline GBR, driving support and over-break costs.
Drill-and-blast and shotcrete crews are nationally scarce; loss of crew to competing project delays heading advance rates.
Cofferdam and diversion works exposed to spring freshet flows exceeding design return period; rebuild of in-river works possible.
ESA-driven in-water work windows of {n_weeks} weeks/year compress diversion, intake, and tailrace construction sequences.
Owner-driven changes to fish passage facility design during construction trigger re-permitting and rework of intake structure.
Ongoing consultation with {tribe} regarding cultural resources may produce mid-construction mitigation requirements.

typical_issues.description_template: Unseasonal flow event overtopped upstream cofferdam; dewatering and inspection in progress.
Class IV/V rock encountered in tunnel; rock-bolt and shotcrete quantities trending {pct}% over baseline.
Repeat NDE rejections on penstock circumferential welds; welder qualification under review.
Resource agency rejected fish screen approach velocity calculation; revised design under expedited review.
Mass concrete pour exceeded thermal control plan limits; engineering disposition pending.
Controlled blasting tolerance exceeded in tailrace; remediation grouting required.
Transport damage to runner detected at site; vendor repair plan under review.
Storm event washed out site access road; alternative routing impacting deliveries.
Turbidity downstream exceeded NPDES limit during diversion works; regulator notified.
Specialty heavy-haul permit delays generator stator delivery to powerhouse.

typical_co_drivers: Geotechnical variance triggering tunnel support class change
Resource agency-driven fish passage design modifications
Client-directed capacity uprate or runner design change
Extended in-water work window restrictions
Flood event recovery and cofferdam reconstruction

description: Binary ORC geothermal plants tied to a producer/injector well field, typically EPC scope from wellhead tie-in through plant and step-up substation. Resource risk is usually carved out, but plant performance under varying resource conditions is a core engineering risk.

typical_risks.description_template: Binary cycle ORC modules supplied by a single OEM ({orc_oem}); factory schedule slip directly impacts mechanical completion.
BLM lease and state geothermal permit impose mitigation requirements that may be revised mid-construction.
Actual production well enthalpy may differ from owner-furnished resource basis, impacting heat exchanger sizing and net output guarantees.
High-temp / sour-service piping welding crews in {region} are scarce; productivity loss likely during peak mechanical phase.
Pentane/isobutane working fluid handling triggers PSM/RMP-equivalent controls; non-conformance during commissioning causes delay.
Plant site at elevation {elev_ft} ft subject to winter access constraints, compressing concrete and outdoor mechanical work.
Owner-directed change in cooling configuration (air-cooled vs hybrid) during detailed design impacts heat rejection package and footprint.

typical_issues.description_template: Factory acceptance test of ORC turbo-generator skid failed vibration limits; vendor remediation in progress.
Initial production test flows below resource basis; resizing of plant inlet manifold under evaluation.
Non-condensable gas H2S concentrations exceeded design basis; abatement skid sizing being revisited.
ACC fan vibration during run-in exceeded acceptance; gearbox alignment investigation underway.
QC audit found insulation system thickness below spec on geothermal fluid piping; rework scope being scoped.
Minor hydrocarbon working-fluid leak during commissioning triggered area evacuation and re-inspection.
GSU transformer ex-works date slipped, impacting energisation milestone.
Battery limit between drilling contractor and EPC at wellhead under dispute; resolution required to close mechanical interfaces.
High winds damaged installed weather jacketing; repairs scheduled.
Performance test net output {pct}% below guarantee; cause analysis on ambient correction underway.

typical_co_drivers: Resource basis revision after additional well testing
Owner-directed cooling system reconfiguration
H2S/NCG abatement scope additions
Plant capacity uprate post-FEED
Permit-driven environmental mitigation additions

subsegment: Municipal drinking water treatment plant (20-100 MGD)
description: Conventional or membrane-based municipal water treatment, often design-build or progressive design-build for municipal utility clients. Schedule is bounded by consent-decree compliance dates and the need to maintain finished-water delivery throughout construction.
hard_deadline_themes: Safe Drinking Water Act regulatory milestone

typical_risks.description_template: Sole-source membrane modules from {membrane_oem} or specialty UV reactors create concentration risk on a critical-path package.
EPA/state consent decree imposes hard regulatory deadline of {decree_date}; stipulated penalties accrue daily on slip.
Existing plant site has documented buried utilities, abandoned structures, and potential contamination not fully characterised pre-bid.
Process instrumentation and SCADA integration labour in {region} is constrained; commissioning ramp at risk.
Maintaining continuous finished-water delivery requires limited shutdown windows, each requiring 60+ day owner notification.
Site earthworks in {region} are sensitive to wet-season precipitation; multiple wet-weather shutdowns possible during foundation phase.
Municipal owner adds resilience or treatment scope (e.g., PFAS, ozone) mid-project in response to emerging regulation.

typical_issues.description_template: Excavation struck unmapped utility; work paused pending utility owner coordination.
Membrane skid factory schedule slipped by {n_weeks} weeks; commissioning sequence re-planned.
Hairline cracks in basin walls detected during hydrostatic test; repair and re-test scheduled.
SCADA point-to-point testing identified {n_points} non-conformances; integrator remediation in progress.
Commissioning runs produced DBP levels above target; chemistry adjustment trials underway.
Planned tie-in shutdown could not proceed due to upstream system condition; rescheduling required.
Petroleum-impacted soil discovered during excavation; characterisation and disposal scoping underway.
Generator load bank test failed acceptance; vendor returning for tuning.
Sodium hypochlorite feed line leak during commissioning; containment and material review in progress.
Operator training curriculum lagging plant turnover schedule; risk to substantial completion.

typical_co_drivers: Differing subsurface conditions (contamination, buried structures)
Owner-directed treatment process additions (PFAS, ozone, GAC)
Regulatory rule changes during construction
Tie-in sequence revisions to maintain water delivery
Resilience / seismic scope upgrades

description: Coastal SWRO plants delivering municipal or industrial water, with intake/outfall marine works and high-pressure RO trains. Marine permitting, brine outfall compliance, and energy-recovery device performance are the dominant risk drivers.
hard_deadline_themes: Coastal Zone Management Act / state coastal commission approvals

typical_risks.description_template: Energy recovery devices and RO membranes from {oem} concentrate technology risk; ERD performance shortfalls directly hit specific energy consumption guarantee.
Brine outfall NPDES and coastal commission conditions may be appealed by third parties, deferring marine work start.
Intake and outfall tunnel/pipeline alignment may encounter variable seabed conditions, requiring micro-tunnel method changes.
Specialist marine contractors for intake/outfall installation are globally scarce; mobilisation slip cascades into entire schedule.
Marine construction confined to {n_months}-month seasonal weather window; missing the window pushes outfall completion by a full year.
Brine diffuser dilution performance under operating conditions may not meet permit, triggering redesign and re-permitting.
Owner-driven changes to product water specification (boron, hardness) require additional post-treatment stages.

typical_issues.description_template: Third-party appeal of coastal commission approval delaying marine NTP.
Frac-out during HDD intake installation triggered regulatory notification and method review.
Outfall diffuser fabrication slipped, jeopardising marine installation window.
Initial membrane element lot failed integrity tests; replacement shipment in progress.
Pretreatment SDI exceeded design; pretreatment chemistry being revisited.
HP pump alignment issues found during string testing; vendor field service mobilised.
Concrete batch rejected for chloride exposure non-conformance; mix design revision underway.
Marine mammal observer triggered work stoppage for protected species in zone.
Regulator requested additional plume modelling; resubmission required before commissioning.
Performance test SEC exceeded contractual guarantee by {pct}%; ERD tuning and membrane condition investigation in progress.

typical_co_drivers: Marine permit conditions adding mitigation scope
Differing marine subsurface conditions during HDD/tunneling
Owner-directed post-treatment additions for product water spec
Capacity uprate or train addition post-NTP
Schedule acceleration to recover marine season slip

subsegment: Large-diameter water conveyance pipeline / tunnel (60-120 inch, 10-40 miles)
description: Major water transmission projects involving large-diameter steel or PCCP pipeline, micro-tunneling under road/rail/river crossings, and pump stations. Schedule and cost risk are concentrated in geotechnical variance and right-of-way coordination.

typical_risks.description_template: Large-diameter steel or PCCP pipe mill capacity is constrained nationally; competing megaprojects may displace delivery slots.
Section 404 and state stream-crossing permits subject to seasonal restrictions and conditions that may be issued late.
Crossings under {n_crossings} road/rail/river alignments expose project to differing-site-conditions claims if rock or groundwater conditions vary from GBR.
Owner-furnished easements across {n_parcels} parcels may not be timely; condemnation timelines outside EPC control.
Large-diameter pipe welding crews are scarce; competing pipeline projects in {region} compress regional supply.
Open-cut corridor work sensitive to wet-season conditions; trench wall stability and dewatering costs may escalate.
Railroad crossing agreement conditions and DOT lane closure windows constrain crossing sequence and timing.

typical_issues.description_template: Owner-furnished easement for parcel {parcel_id} not delivered; crew demobilised from segment.
MTBM struck boulder field at crossing {crossing_id}; rescue shaft under evaluation.
Field-applied coating failed holiday testing on multiple joints; rework in progress.
Hydrotest segment failed pressure hold; investigation isolating leak location.
Artifact discovered during trenching; SHPO consultation paused work in affected reach.
Construction dewatering discharge exceeded turbidity limit; corrective action required.
Vertical turbine pump delivery slipped, impacting pump station commissioning.
Railroad flagger availability constrained crossing work to limited windows.
Localised trench wall failure after rain event; OSHA review and re-shoring required.
WPS qualification gap for specific pipe-to-fitting combination identified late; qualification testing scheduled.

typical_co_drivers: Differing subsurface conditions at crossings
Easement / right-of-way delays driving sequence changes
Permit-driven alignment modifications
Owner-directed alignment or scope changes (added connections)
Acceleration to meet drought-response delivery date

subsegment: Integrated or mini-mill modernisation (caster, reheat furnace, rolling mill upgrade)
description: Brownfield modernisation of operating steel facilities, including caster replacement, furnace re-line, mill upgrades, and emissions controls. Schedule risk is dominated by the production turnaround window and live-plant interface management.
hard_deadline_themes: EPA Title V air permit compliance

typical_risks.description_template: Caster / mill packages from {oem} (e.g., SMS, Primetals, Danieli) on critical path; OEM field service availability for commissioning is constrained.
Outage window of {n_weeks} weeks is owner-fixed and tied to order book; any slip causes LDs and lost production claims.
Existing structure, foundation, and utility as-builts unreliable; interferences typically discovered during demolition phase.
Refractory masons, millwrights, and high-voltage electricians available only through narrow regional pool during turnaround windows.
Adjacent operating units expose work face to hot work, molten metal, and confined space hazards; LOTO and permit-to-work compliance critical.
Emissions control upgrades must demonstrate compliance per consent agreement; stack test failure triggers operational restrictions.
Owner adjusts product mix or grade specifications mid-project, driving changes to mill stand, cooling, or coating scope.

typical_issues.description_template: Demolition uncovered unmapped structural ties to adjacent operating bay; engineering disposition pending.
Specialty refractory shipment delayed; furnace re-line sequence at risk.
Wind speeds exceeded crane plan limits during heavy lift; sequence rescheduled.
Hand injury recordable during pipe-fitting in confined area; stand-down and JHA refresh completed.
Particle count out of spec after mill hydraulic flush; extended flush required.
Caster cold commissioning identified mould oscillation defects; vendor field engineering on site.
Initial stack test on baghouse exceeded particulate limit; tuning and re-test required.
Owner requested two-week outage extension; commercial impact under negotiation.
EOT crane runway survey exceeded tolerance; shim adjustments and re-survey scheduled.
First-coil yield below ramp curve; process tuning and OEM support ongoing.

typical_co_drivers: Brownfield interferences and unforeseen demolition scope
Owner-directed product mix or grade changes
Outage window extension or compression
Emissions control scope additions per regulator
Acceleration to recover from turnaround slippage

subsegment: Specialty chemicals plant — greenfield or major expansion (200-2000 TPD)
description: Greenfield or expansion specialty chemical plants (e.g., polymers, intermediates, electronic-grade chemicals) executed as fixed-price or reimbursable EPC. Schedule risks center on long-lead equipment, PSM compliance, and licensor coordination.
hard_deadline_themes: Title V air permit construction approval

typical_risks.description_template: Process licensor {licensor} controls reactor and key proprietary equipment delivery; FAT slips directly drive mechanical completion.
PSSR closure under OSHA PSM is gate to startup; documentation gaps commonly delay first feed by 2-6 weeks.
Site investigation may understate variability in soil bearing or groundwater across {n_acres}-acre plot, driving foundation rework.
Stainless and exotic-alloy welders and instrument fitters are nationally scarce; productivity and rework rates highly sensitive.
Gulf Coast or Southeast site location exposes outdoor construction and modules to hurricane-season disruption.
Licensor PFD revisions or owner capacity uprates during detailed engineering propagate piping, electrical, and structural rework.
First chemical introduction involves toxic/flammable hazards; any deviation triggers lengthy MOC and risk review.

typical_issues.description_template: Reactor vessel ex-works slipped {n_weeks} weeks due to fabricator NDE rework; mechanical completion at risk.
Pipe weld NDE rejection rate trending above {pct}%; welder qualification audit and remediation underway.
Site secured for tropical storm; {n_days} days lost and post-event inspection required.
Pipe rack module sustained transit damage; field repair plan under review.
Management of Change backlog exceeds {n_items}; risk to PSSR closure schedule.
High-pressure piping circuit failed hydrotest; isolation and repair underway.
Loop check identified DCS configuration errors across {n_loops} loops; controls integrator on site.
Cooling tower fill defects discovered during commissioning; vendor remediation required.
Construction-phase fugitive emissions tracking approaching permit limit; controls being augmented.
Initial product samples off-spec on {parameter}; licensor support engaged for diagnostic.

typical_co_drivers: Licensor PFD/P&ID revisions
Owner-directed capacity uprate
Differing site conditions at foundations
Hurricane recovery and schedule mitigation
Scope additions for emissions / PSM compliance

subsegment: Combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) plant — 500-1100 MW (1x1 or 2x1)
description: Greenfield or repower CCGT plants with F- or H-class gas turbines, HRSGs, and steam turbine. Fixed-price EPC with OEM-supplied power island; schedule and commercial risk dominated by gas turbine delivery, interconnection, and capacity market commitments.

typical_risks.description_template: Critical-path gas turbine and generator supply from {oem} (GE Vernova, Mitsubishi Power, Siemens Energy); global delivery queue creates limited recovery options on slip.
ISO interconnection agreement and capacity market commitment impose hard COD; LDs and replacement capacity cost on slip.
Site geotechnical may reveal soft soils or shallow groundwater requiring deep foundations under HRSG and STG pedestals.
HRSG erection and large-bore piping crews are nationally scarce during peak season; competing CCGT and industrial projects compress supply.
PSD/Title V permit may impose stack height, emissions limits, or operating restrictions that propagate to design changes.
Outdoor construction, HRSG erection, and transformer setting exposed to seasonal severe weather in {region}.
Owner-directed duct firing addition, fuel flexibility, or hydrogen-blending readiness scope drives engineering rework.
Gas lateral delivery date is outside EPC control; pipeline slip prevents first-fire and performance testing.

typical_issues.description_template: Gas turbine ex-works slipped {n_weeks} weeks; commissioning sequence rebaselined.
HRSG harp pressure-test leak identified; repair in progress.
Steam turbine alignment outside OEM tolerance; recheck after foundation grout cure.
GSU DGA results elevated during energisation; vendor investigation underway.
Gas pipeline interconnect in-service date slipped; first-fire deferred.
ACC fan and gearbox vibration during commissioning out of spec; tuning ongoing.
HRSG chemistry excursion during steam blow-out; cleanup required.
Near-miss during HRSG modular lift; standdown and lift-plan review completed.
CEMS RATA failed certification; instrument vendor on site.
Net heat rate test exceeded guarantee by {pct}%; corrections and re-test under evaluation.

typical_co_drivers: OEM GT delivery slippage and acceleration response
Owner-directed duct firing or hydrogen-readiness additions
Air permit conditions driving design changes
Gas pipeline interconnect delay mitigation
Differing site conditions at major equipment foundations
